card.summary_en: A 1909 essay in which Bak Eun-sik names three causes of Confucianism's decline (ruler-centredness, passively waiting for students, rambling scholarship) and calls for reform.

notes.ko:
**저자** 박은식(朴殷植, 1859–1925)은 황해도 황주 출신으로, 호는 겸곡(謙谷)·백암(白巖)이다. 젊어서는 주자학을 공부한 유학자였고, 1890년대 말부터 독립협회와 『황성신문』, 이어 『대한매일신보』 등에서 논설을 쓰며 개신(개혁) 유학자·애국계몽 운동가로 활동했다. 서북학회에도 관여했다. 1910년 국권 피탈 뒤에는 중국으로 망명하여 『한국통사』(1915), 『한국독립운동지혈사』(1920)를 썼고, 1925년에는 대한민국 임시정부 제2대 대통령에 선출되었으나 같은 해 11월에 세상을 떠났다. 정치적으로는 문화적·역사적 민족주의자이자 개화·계몽 성향의 유교 개혁론자로 분류되며, 후기에는 독립운동의 중심에 섰다. 친일 활동으로 알려진 바는 없다.

**시대적 맥락** 1905년 을사늑약으로 외교권을 잃고 1907년 정미7조약으로 내정까지 일본의 통제를 받게 된 뒤, 국권 회복을 위한 계몽·교육 운동이 활발했다. 이 글은 1909년 합병(1910) 직전에 쓰였고, 유교가 망국의 책임을 지는 낡은 학문이라는 비판에 대해 유교 스스로 변해야 한다는 답을 내놓은 글이다. 박은식은 같은 시기 유교 개혁 단체인 대동교(大同敎)를 세우는 일에도 관여했다고 알려져 있다.

**배경** 『서북학회월보』 제10호(1909년경)에 '겸곡생'이라는 필명으로 실렸다. 여기에 쓴 텍스트는 국사편찬위원회 한국사데이터베이스의 전사본이며, 국한문 혼용문이다. 전사 과정에서 '하'가 빠진 곳이 있다(예: '如히'는 '如하이', '不得 其 門하면'의 '不得'은 '不得하고'의 뜻). 번역은 의도된 뜻을 따랐다.

**의의** 유교의 쇠퇴 원인을 안에서 분석하고 구체적 처방(민중 지향, 적극적 포교, 간이한 공부법으로서 양명학)을 제시한 근대 한국 유교 개혁론의 대표 문헌으로 평가된다. 주자학 독존에 대한 비판과 양명학 추천은 이후 박은식의 사상과 한국 양명학 연구에 영향을 주었다.

**형식과 주제** 세 가지 문제를 차례로 제기하는 논설체이며, 고전 인용과 역사 사례(진·한, 원헌, 관녕, 조헌)로 논증하고 불교·기독교와 비교한다. 주제는 군주 중심에서 민중 중심으로, 앉아서 기다림에서 나아가 가르침으로, 번쇄한 학문에서 간단직절한 학문으로의 전환이다.

**읽기 도움**
- 斯文(사문): 유교 문화·학문
- 末流(말류): 후대의 흐름, 폐단
- 匪我求童蒙(비아구동몽): 『주역』 몽괘, '내가 어린 사람을 찾는 것이 아니다'
- 轍環列國(철환열국): 수레로 여러 나라를 돌아다님
- 致良知(치양지)·知行合一(지행합일): 왕양명의 핵심 개념
- 黨錮(당고)·士禍(사화): 선비 탄압 사건
- 一網打盡(일망타진): 한꺼번에 모두 잡음
- 어미: -하노라(문어체 평서), -할지어다(명령), -이뇨 ~인가
notes.en:
**About the author** Bak Eun-sik (1859–1925; pen names Gyeomgok and Baegam) was born in Hwanghae Province (Hwangju). He began as a Neo-Confucian scholar and from the late 1890s wrote for the Independence Club, the Hwangseong Sinmun and then the Daehan Maeil Sinbo as a reform-minded Confucian and patriotic-enlightenment activist; he was also involved in the Northwestern (Seobuk) Society. After the annexation of 1910 he went into exile in China, where he wrote the Hanguk tongsa (1915) and Hanguk dongnip undong jihyeolsa (1920), and in 1925 he was elected second president of the Provisional Government, dying the same year. Politically he is classed as a cultural and historical nationalist and an enlightenment-minded reformer of Confucianism who later stood at the centre of the independence movement. No collaboration with Japan is known.

**Historical context** After the 1905 protectorate treaty took away Korea's diplomatic rights and the 1907 treaty put internal affairs under Japanese control, enlightenment and education movements for national recovery flourished. This essay was written shortly before the 1910 annexation, answering the charge that Confucianism was an outdated learning responsible for the nation's fall by arguing that Confucianism itself must change. Bak is said to have been involved at about the same time in founding the Confucian reform body Daedonggyo.

**Background** It appeared under the pen name "Gyeomgok-saeng" in the Seobuk hakhoe wolbo no. 10 (c. 1909). The text used here is the National Institute of Korean History database transcription, in mixed Hanja-Hangul prose. In transcription some hangul "ha" (하) has dropped out (for example "如히" stands for "如하이", and "不得" in "不得 其 門하면" for "不得하고"); the translation follows the intended sense.

**Significance** It is regarded as a representative document of modern Korean Confucian reform thought: it analyses the causes of Confucianism's decline from within and prescribes concrete remedies (orientation to the common people, active outreach, and Wang Yangming's learning as a simple method). Its criticism of the monopoly of Zhu Xi learning and its advocacy of Yangming learning shaped Bak's later thought and the study of Korean Yangming learning.

**Form and themes** An argumentative essay raising three problems in turn, supported by classical quotations and historical cases (Qin and Han, Yuan Xian, Guan Ning, Jo Heon) and comparison with Buddhism and Christianity. Its themes are the shift from ruler-centred to people-centred Confucianism, from waiting to be sought to going out to teach, and from rambling scholarship to simple and direct learning.

**Reading help**
- 斯文 (samun): Confucian culture and learning
- 末流 (malryu): later currents, abuses
- 匪我求童蒙: from the Hexagram Meng of the Changes, "it is not I who seek the ignorant youth"
- 轍環列國: travelling round the states by chariot
- 致良知 and 知行合一: Wang Yangming's core ideas
- 黨錮 and 士禍: persecutions of scholars
- 一網打盡: to catch all at one cast
- Endings: -하노라 (I do, literary), -할지어다 (imperative), -이뇨 (is it?)

paragraphs.en: On the Need to Renew Confucianism, by Gyeomgok-saeng ("Student Gyeomgok", the pen name of Bak Eun-sik)

paragraphs.orig: 夫我 東洋數千年 敎化界에 中正純粹ᄒᆞ고 廣大精微ᄒᆞ야 列聖이 傳授ᄒᆞ고 群賢이 講明ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 儒敎가 終是 印度의 釋迦敎와 西洋의 基督敎와 如히 世界에 大發展을 不得ᄒᆞᆷ은 何故이며 近世에 至ᄒᆞ야 寢微不振이 極度에 達ᄒᆞ야 殆히 來復의 望이 無ᄒᆞᆫ 것은 又 何故이뇨. 余ᄂᆞᆫ 大韓 儒敎界에 一分子라. 我의 祖先과 我의 平生이 孔子의 恩賜를 受홈이 莫大ᄒᆞᆫᄃᆡ 現今 孔子의 敎가 日就黯淡ᄒᆞ고 日益凜綴ᄒᆞᆫ 景況을 對ᄒᆞ야 匪直懍然而 懼라. 實惕然發汗ᄒᆞᆷ이 有ᄒᆞᆫ 故로 其 原因을 溯考ᄒᆞ며 末流을 推測ᄒᆞ니儒敎界에 三大 問題가 有ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 該 三大 問題에 就ᄒᆞ야 改良求新을 不爲ᄒᆞ면 我儒敎ᄂᆞᆫ 不惟不能興旺이라. 究竟滅絶을 不免ᄒᆞᆯ지니 天이 斯文을 喪코져 아니ᄒᆞ실진ᄃᆡ 此 問題에 對ᄒᆞ야 改良求新ᄒᆞᆫ 豪傑之士가 出ᄒᆞᆯ지나 我 大韓 世界에 在ᄒᆞ야 儒林의 現況을 觀察ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ此를 改良求新ᄒᆞᆯ 識見과 魄力이 有ᄒᆞᆫ 者를 姑未得見이로다. 嗚呼라 疾痛이 方劇에 狂言이 自發이오. 窮到極處에 自力을 宜奮이라 寧其得罪於諸先輩ᄒᆞ고 取怒於儒林派언졍 不忍使吾孔子之道로 終焉墜地而己라. 於是乎 敢히 不韙을 犯ᄒᆞ고 三大問題를 擧ᄒᆞ야 改良求新의 意見ᄅᆞᆯ 呈ᄒᆞ노라.

paragraphs.en: Confucianism has been upright and pure, vast and subtle in the sphere of teaching and civilisation in East Asia for several thousand years, handed down by the successive sages and expounded by a host of worthies. Why, then, has it never come to flourish greatly throughout the world, as Indian Buddhism and Western Christianity have? And why, in recent times, has it sunk into decline and torpor to the utmost degree, so that there is almost no hope of its revival? I am one member of the Confucian world of Korea. My ancestors and I myself, all our lives, have received Confucius's bounty in immeasurable measure; and when I look at the present condition of Confucius's teaching, which grows dimmer by the day and more threadbare with each passing day, I am not merely awed and afraid: I truly break into a startled sweat. So I have traced back its causes and surveyed its later currents, and I find that the Confucian world has three great problems. If reform and renewal are not carried out on these three problems, our Confucianism will not merely fail to flourish; it will in the end be unable to escape extinction. If Heaven does not wish to destroy this culture (斯文), then heroes who will reform and renew on these problems will surely arise. But when I observe the present state of the Confucian community in Korea, I have so far not seen anyone with the insight and strength to reform and renew it. Alas! When pain is at its sharpest, wild words burst out of themselves; when one is driven to the extreme, one ought to rouse one's own strength. I would rather offend my senior colleagues and provoke the anger of the Confucian faction than bear to let the Way of our Confucius fall at last to the ground. Therefore I dare to commit this wrong, and I raise the three great problems and offer my views on reform and renewal.

paragraphs.orig: 所謂 三大問題는 何也오 一은 儒敎派의 精神이 專히 帝王側에 在ᄒᆞ고 人民社會에 普及ᄒᆞᆯ 精神이 不足홈이오 一은 轍環列國ᄒᆞ야 思易天下의 主義ᄅᆞᆯ 不講ᄒᆞ고 匪我求童蒙이라. 童蒙이 求我라ᄂᆞᆫ 主義ᄅᆞᆯ 是守홈이오 一은 我韓儒家에서 簡易直切ᄒᆞᆫ 法門을 不要ᄒᆞ고 支離汗漫ᄒᆞᆫ 工夫를 專尙ᄒᆞᆷ이라. 第一問題는 維何오 蓋 孔子의 大同之義와 孟子의 民爲重之說로 觀ᄒᆞ면 實로 人民에게 普及ᄒᆞᆫ 精神이 有ᄒᆞᆫ 者이나 孔子ㅣ 歿ᄒᆞ신 後에 諸子가 分處 各國ᄒᆞ야 或 微言을 傳ᄒᆞ고 或 大義을 傅ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫᄃᆡ 孟子ᄂᆞᆫ 民爲重의 義를 發明ᄒᆞ고 苟卿은 尊君權의 義를 表出ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 孟子의 徒ᄂᆞᆫ 鄒 魯之間에 在ᄒᆞ야 其 傳이 遂絶ᄒᆞ고 荀子의 徒ᄂᆞᆫ 自趙至楚ᄒᆞ야 其 傳이 頗廣ᄒᆞ니 李斯가 荀子의 徒로 秦에 入ᄒᆞ야 其術을 用ᄒᆞᆯᄉᆡ 大貪權勢ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 秦始皇의 意ᄅᆞᆯ 迎合ᄒᆞ야 尊君權의 義를 獻ᄒᆞ고 愚民之術를 行ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 當時 秦 漢之間에 儒術로 名ᄒᆞᆫ 者가 皆 荀學의 派라. 漢太祖가 草野에 在ᄒᆞᆯ 時에ᄂᆞᆫ 儒者의 禮節을 嫌惡ᄒᆞ야 其 冠을 溲ᄒᆞ얏스나 及其 帝王의 位에 卽ᄒᆞ야ᄂᆞᆫ 不得不 儒者의 禮儀節文을 取ᄒᆞ야 天下臣民을 御ᄒᆞᆯ지라. 於是에 太牢로 孔子를 祀ᄒᆞ며 陸賈叔孫通의 徒를 收用ᄒᆞᆯ 것이니 何甞孔子의 道德을 深知ᄒᆞ고 景慕ᄒᆞ야 然ᄒᆞᆫ 者리오. 自是로 歷代帝王이 六經을 表章ᄒᆞ야 儒臣을 重用ᄒᆞᆫ 것이 皆 儒敎의 禮節과 名分을 愛ᄒᆞ야 孔子를 尊홈이 卽 其 所有地位를 尊홈이라. 若 其 孔子의 道德眞理를 愛ᄒᆞ얏스면 엇지 修齊治平의 實地 事業이 無ᄒᆞ얏스리오. 惟 其 帝王이 儒者를 尊待ᄒᆞᆷ으로 東洋數千年間에 儒敎派가 恒常 尊貴ᄒᆞᆫ 地位를 占有ᄒᆞᆷ이 他敎派의 比擬ᄒᆞᆫ 바 아니라. 於是 儒敎派의 精神도 ᄯᅩᄒᆞᆫ 專히 帝王側에 在ᄒᆞ야 抱道守正의 君子儒ᄂᆞᆫ 登筵講說에 格君心이 第一主義오. 曲學阿世의 小人儒ᄂᆞᆫ 傅會經義ᄒᆞ야 迎合君意가 無上竗訣이 될 ᄲᅮᆫ이오. 人民社會에 普及ᄒᆞ야 民智를 開發ᄒᆞ고 民權을 伸張케 ᄒᆞᆯ 方針은 未有ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 所以로 君上의 際遇를 得ᄒᆞᆯ 時에ᄂᆞᆫ 彈冠結綬의 榮이 有ᄒᆞ나 若 其 政府의 嫌忌와 君上의 踈待를 被ᄒᆞ면 東漢黨錮의 禍와 我朝士禍의 獄이 有ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 若 其 儒敎의 力이 人民社會에 普及ᄒᆞ야 民智를 開發ᄒᆞ고 民權을 伸張케 ᄒᆞᆫ 根基가 有ᄒᆞ얏스면 幾個奸臣輩가 엇지 君上을 慫惥ᄒᆞ야 一網打盡의 毒計를 行ᄒᆞ얏스리오. 且 其 精神이 專히 帝王側에 在ᄒᆞ고 人民社會에 普及치 아니ᄒᆞᆫ 故로 世界上 大發展을 不得ᄒᆞᆷ이니 此ᄂᆞᆫ 孔子之門에 孟子의 學이 不傳ᄒᆞ고 荀卿의 學이 獨傳ᄒᆞ야 斯文과 生民의게 極不幸을 貽ᄒᆞᆫ 一大缺點이라. 而況現今은 民智가 將次 開發되고 民權이 從而伸張ᄒᆞᆯ 時代라. 此 問題에 對ᄒᆞ야 改良求新치 안코난 發達은 尙矣라 保守를 不得ᄒᆞᆯ지니 儒林諸君은 蹈常習故ᄒᆞ야 變通을 不思홈이 可乎아 否乎아 萬一 孔門의 眞個忠臣이 되야 斯文의 功德을 發揮ᄒᆞ고 生民의 幸福을 畀予코져 ᄒᆞᆯ진ᄃᆡ 此를 改良ᄒᆞ야 孟子의 學을 推廣ᄒᆞ야 人民社會에 普及을懋圖ᄒᆞᆯ 것이오.

paragraphs.en: What are the three great problems? The first is that the spirit of the Confucian school lies wholly on the side of emperors and kings, and it lacks a spirit that would spread to the people and to society. The second is that it does not preach the principle of Confucius, who drove his chariot round the states in order to change the world, but guards instead the principle "It is not I who seek the ignorant youth; the ignorant youth seeks me." The third is that Korean Confucians do not demand a simple, direct and incisive gateway to learning, but devote themselves exclusively to fragmentary and rambling effort. What is the first problem? Judged by Confucius's idea of the Great Unity (大同) and Mencius's doctrine that "the people are the most important," Confucianism truly does have a spirit that reaches the people. But after Confucius died, his disciples dispersed to the various states; some transmitted his subtle words and some his great principles. Mencius elucidated the principle that the people are most important, while Xunzi (the text writes the name with a variant character) set forth the principle of honouring the ruler's authority. Mencius's followers remained between Zou and Lu, and their transmission was soon cut off; Xunzi's followers went from Zhao to Chu, and their transmission spread widely. Li Si, as a follower of Xunzi, entered Qin and applied his art there: he catered to the will of the First Emperor of Qin, who craved power, offered him the principle of honouring the ruler's authority, and practised the art of keeping the people ignorant. The men of the Qin and Han period who were famed for Confucian learning were all of Xunzi's school. When the founder of the Han was still among the grass and fields, he loathed the ceremonial manners of Confucians and even urinated in their hats; but once he took the throne, he had no choice but to adopt the Confucians' rites and ceremonial forms in order to rule his subjects. So he sacrificed to Confucius with the grand sacrifice (太牢) and took into service such men as Lu Jia and Shusun Tong; how could that have come from deeply knowing and admiring Confucius's virtue? From then on the emperors of every age displayed the Six Classics and gave heavy responsibilities to Confucian ministers, but they did so because they loved Confucian ceremony and the order of rank, and honouring Confucius meant honouring their own position. Had they loved Confucius's moral truth, how could there have been no real undertakings of self-cultivation, ordering the household, governing the state and bringing peace to the world? Because emperors honoured and favoured Confucians, the Confucian school held an eminent position throughout East Asia for several thousand years, which no other school could match. And so the spirit of the Confucian school, too, lay wholly on the side of the emperor. The gentleman-Confucian, who held to the Way and kept to rectitude, made "rectifying the ruler's mind" in the lecture hall his first principle; the petty Confucian, who bent learning to flatter the age, forced the meaning of the classics and made catering to the ruler's will his supreme secret art, and that was all. There was no policy to spread among the people and society, to develop the people's intelligence and extend the people's rights. Therefore, when they won the ruler's favour they enjoyed the glory of dusting off their caps and tying on their sashes; but when they incurred the government's dislike and the ruler's neglect, there came the calamity of the Eastern Han partisan prohibitions (黨錮) and the prisons of our own dynasty's literati purges (士禍). Had the strength of Confucianism spread among the people so as to develop their intelligence and extend their rights, how could a handful of treacherous ministers have urged the ruler on and carried out a poisonous scheme to catch them all in one net? Moreover, because its spirit lay wholly on the emperor's side and did not spread among the people, Confucianism could not develop greatly in the world. This is that within Confucius's school Mencius's teaching was not transmitted while Xunzi's alone was, which bequeathed the utmost misfortune to the culture and to the people: one great defect. Furthermore, the present is an age in which the people's intelligence is about to be developed and the people's rights are to be extended accordingly. If we do not reform and renew on this question, let alone develop, we shall not even be able to preserve. Is it right, or not, for the gentlemen of the Confucian community to tread the old paths and cling to old habits, never thinking of adaptation? If you truly wish to be loyal servants of the Confucian gate, to bring out the merit of this culture and bestow happiness on the people, then reform this, extend Mencius's teaching, and strive to spread it among the people and society.

Confucius's "changing the world," Shakyamuni's "saving all beings," and Christ's "giving himself for the people" are one in their principle of saving the world. Yet why has our Confucian teaching been unable to develop greatly in the world as Buddhism and Christianity have? Buddhism combined the Mahayana and Hinayana methods and had a scope that applied equally to the wise and the ignorant. The followers of Christianity were extremely broad in the scope of their mission and extremely ardent in sincerity and effort: their footprints spread across the five oceans and six continents to carry the gospel; disregarding the sacrifice of their lives, they even suffered the calamity of being eaten by savage natives, yet after earlier failures later missionaries followed on, until they had attained the goal of their mission. The followers of our Confucianism, by contrast, do not practise Confucius's principle of travelling by chariot through the states to change the world, but cling only to the principle "It is not I who seek the ignorant youth; the ignorant youth seeks me." They bar tight Yuan Xian's jar-mouth window and wear through Guan Ning's wooden couch; they sit waiting for the gifts of students who come to learn, and do not use the wooden-tongued bell that wakes the people. Not only can their teaching not reach the people and society; even their own knowledge falls into narrowness, and they know nothing at all of the state of things and the warnings of the age. How could they bring out the merit of this culture and bestow happiness on the people? This too is one great defect. The present is an age when the doors of the world have opened wide and mankind competes. If we keep to the caves and crags as before and do not go out of doors, the whole vast world will fall into the possession of others; where then shall we go to transmit our Way? Such dead methods ought to be reformed and methods of advance put into practice. Formerly Master Jo Jungbong (Jo Heon) took Yi I's Gyeongmong yogyeol with him, and even to ordinary travellers at roadside inns he would urge reading and explain it. Confucians of today, too, must have this sincere zeal and this living method if they are to maintain the culture.

paragraphs.en: What is the third problem? In terms of the scope of our Way, it covers as heaven covers and bears as earth bears, and nothing great or small, coarse or fine, is lacking; yet the entry point of its discipline (the text reads "eight-head", probably a slip for "entry-head") must be a single path. The Book of Changes says, "With ease and simplicity the principles of the world are grasped." Confucius said, "I have one thread that runs through all." Mencius said, "First establish what is greater." Master Cheng said, "If what one keeps is not concise, one overflows and achieves nothing." Mr. Fan said, "The student must strive to know the essentials; knowing the essentials suffices to exhaust the breadth." Thus knowing the root is the way to know the essentials, and knowing the essentials is the way to exhaust the breadth. If a student has no will for fundamental learning, there is no need to discuss the matter; but if he has the will and cannot find the gate, he will find it hard, be tired of its tedium, and in the end give it up. How much more so today, when the sciences grow more complex day by day and human enterprise grows swifter and nimbler day by day.

paragraphs.orig: 至於本領學問에도 簡易直切ᄒᆞᆫ 法門을 不要ᄒᆞ고 支離汗漫ᄒᆞᆫ 工夫에 從事ᄒᆞ라 ᄒᆞ면 後進 靑年이 皆苦其難而厭其煩ᄒᆞ야 下手을 不肯ᄒᆞᆯ지니 此는 吾儒敎界에 實노 重要ᄒᆞᆫ 問題라. 蓋 我國六百年間에 全國士林이 奉爲泰斗라 ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 前輩諸先生의 傳授宗旨는 皆朱子의 學이라. 若其 朱學外에 別立邪說者면 斯門亂賊의 名을 被ᄒᆞ고 一般 儒者가 皆以異端邪說로 指斥ᄒᆞᆫ 故로 朱學以外에ᄂᆞᆫ 更히 學派가 無ᄒᆞᆫ지라. 余도 自幼受書에 朱書를 誦讀ᄒᆞ고 朱說을 篤守ᄒᆞ얏스니 古來諸儒中에 惟是朱子의 恩賜를 受ᄒᆞᆷ이 最多ᄒᆞ도다. 蓋朱子의 學이 地負海涵ᄒᆞ야 無所不該ᄒᆞ니 其有功於聖門이 偉大ᄒᆞ고 垂惠於後學이 盛多ᄒᆞ니 曷敢妄哉며 曷敢論哉아 然이나 後之儒者가 朱子의 聰明과 魄力과 勤篤이 無ᄒᆞ고ᄂᆞᆫ 其 涯涘를 窺及지 못ᄒᆞ야 年紀가 忽己蹉跎에 實地見得과 實地成就가 未有할지니 其如之何오. 朱子曰 象物之表裏精粗ㅣ 無不到而吾心之全體大用이無不明矣라 ᄒᆞ얏스니 今日 吾人爲學이 衆物의 表裏精粗가 無不到ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 境遇ᄅᆞᆯ 待ᄒᆞ야 吾心의 體用이 無不明ᄒᆞᆫ다 할진ᄃᆡ 人生一世에 光陰이 幾何오 終身用力할지라도 卒業할 期限이 無할 것이오 學問의 卒業할 期限이 無ᄒᆞᆫ則 엇지 事業을 做得할 餘日이 有ᄒᆞ리오 此ᄂᆞᆫ 學者의 可能ᄒᆞᆯ 바 아니라 故로 朱子ㅣ 晩年에 曰 多識前言往行이 固君子所急이나 近因反求ᄒᆞ야 未得 安穩處ᄒᆞ니 却始知前此에 未免支離라 ᄒᆞ고 又 曰 某ㅣ 近日에 亦覺向來說話가 有太支離處라 反身以求에 正坐自己用功이 亦未切耳라 ᄒᆞ고 又有詩 曰 向來枉費推移力터니 此日中流自在行이라 ᄒᆞ얏스니 此ᄂᆞᆫ 朱子ㅣ 於本原上 工夫에 蓋 三致意焉者라. 後之儒者가 但其 浩瀚森列ᄒᆞᆫ 言論文字에 從事ᄒᆞ면 本原上實見得이 豈不難哉아 且 現時代 學問은 各種 科學이 卽 格物窮理의 工夫니 智育의 事오 至於心理學ᄒᆞ야ᄂᆞᆫ 德育의 事니 不可混作 一串工夫라 今에 朱子의 言論文字ᄅᆞᆯ 將ᄒᆞ야 後進靑年에게 傳授코져 ᄒᆞ면 其 浩如淵海ᄒᆞᆫ 것을 見ᄒᆞ고 開卷을 不待ᄒᆞ야 苦難厭煩의 意가 生할 것이오 況天下事業이 日出不窮ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 時代ᄅᆞᆯ 當ᄒᆞ야 許多歲月을 費了ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 工夫에ᄂᆞᆫ 下手키 實難ᄒᆞ도다. 然則 今之儒者가 各種 科學 外에 本領學問을 求ᄒᆞ고져 ᄒᆞᆯ진ᄃᆡ 陽明學에 從事ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 것이 實노 簡單切要ᄒᆞᆫ 法門이라. 蓋 致良知의 學은 直指本心ᄒᆞ야 超凡入聖ᄒᆞᄂᆞᆫ 門路오 知行合一은 在於心術之微에 省察法이 緊切ᄒᆞ고 在於事物應用에 果敢力이 活潑ᄒᆞ니 此ᄂᆞᆫ 陽明學派의 氣節과 事業의 特著ᄒᆞᆫ 功效가 實多ᄒᆞᆫ 所以라. 嗚呼라 後生淺見으로 何敢朱學王學의 辨을 作ᄒᆞ야學界上 一大 公案을 惹起ᄒᆞ리오만은 將來 後進學界를 觀察ᄒᆞ건ᄃᆡ 簡單直切ᄒᆞᆫ 法門이 無ᄒᆞ고난 孔孟之學에 從事할 者ㅣ 幾希ᄒᆞᆯ지니 大抵 朱學王學이 其爲孔孟之徒ᄂᆞᆫ 一也라. 何舍何擇이리오 吾孔孟의 道로 ᄒᆞ여곰 其 傳을 不失코져 ᄒᆞ면 不得不簡單直切ᄒᆞᆫ 法門으로 後進을 指示ᄒᆞᆷ이 可ᄒᆞ도다.

paragraphs.en: Even in fundamental learning, if students are told to take up a rambling, diffuse discipline without a simple, direct and incisive method, young juniors will all find it hard and be sick of its tedium and unwilling to begin. This is a truly important problem for our Confucian world. For six hundred years in our country, the transmitted teaching of the forebears whom the whole body of scholars has revered as their Mount Tai and Big Dipper has been wholly the learning of Master Zhu (Zhu Xi). Anyone who set up a deviant doctrine outside Zhu's learning bore the name of a traitor to the Confucian gate and was denounced by all Confucians as heterodox, so apart from Zhu's learning there was no other school. I too, from childhood when I received my books, recited Zhu's writings and firmly held to Zhu's views; of all the Confucians of the past, I have received the most from Master Zhu. Master Zhu's learning is as vast as the earth carrying and the sea containing, and nothing is left out; his merit toward the sage's gate is great, and the favour he bestowed on later students is abundant. How dare I be presumptuous, how dare I discuss him? Yet later Confucians, lacking Master Zhu's intelligence, strength and diligence, cannot even glimpse his shores; the years slip by in waste, and real insight and real achievement do not come. What is to be done? Master Zhu said, "When the inside and outside, the fine and coarse, of things are all reached, then the whole substance and great function of my mind will be without fail clear" (the text writes "象物", probably a slip for "衆物"). If our study today must wait until the inside and outside, fine and coarse of all things are reached and the substance and function of my mind are clear, how long is a human life? Even if one strives one's whole life, there will be no date of graduation; and if there is no date of graduation for learning, what spare days will there be to accomplish anything? This is not within the power of a student. Therefore in his old age Master Zhu said, "Knowing much of former words and deeds is indeed what a gentleman urgently needs; but recently, turning back to seek within, I have not found a settled place, and I now first realise that I did not escape fragmentation before." And again, "I too recently feel that what I used to say was overly fragmented; turning to seek within myself, I see that my own effort too was not incisive." And he also wrote in a poem, "Formerly I wasted my strength pushing and shoving; today, in midstream, I move freely." So Master Zhu himself gave repeated attention to effort at the original root. If later Confucians merely devote themselves to his vast, densely arrayed writings, how hard it will be to gain real insight at the root! Moreover, in the learning of the present age the various sciences are the work of investigating things and exhausting principle, a matter of intellectual education, whereas the study of the mind is a matter of moral education; they must not be mixed together into one string of effort. If one tries now to pass on Master Zhu's writings to young juniors, they will see them vast as an ocean and, before even opening a book, will feel hardship and weariness; and in an age when undertakings emerge endlessly, it is truly hard to begin a discipline that spends so many years. Then, if the Confucians of today wish to seek fundamental learning in addition to the sciences, devoting oneself to the learning of Wang Yangming is truly the simple and essential method. The learning of "extending innate knowledge" points directly at the original mind and is a gateway to transcend the ordinary and enter sagehood; the "unity of knowledge and action" provides a keen method of self-examination in the subtle workings of the mind and a lively resolute force in the handling of affairs. This is why the Yangming school has many notable effects in integrity and achievement. Alas! How dare I, a junior of shallow views, raise the matter of Zhu learning versus Wang learning and stir a great public case in the learning world? But looking at the learning world of the future, without a simple and direct method there will be few who engage in the learning of Confucius and Mencius. Zhu learning and Wang learning are alike disciples of Confucius and Mencius. Why discard one and choose the other? If we wish the Way of Confucius and Mencius not to lose its transmission, we have no choice but to point the juniors to a simple and direct method, and that is right.

paragraphs.orig: 嗚呼라 以上 三大 問題에 關ᄒᆞ야 多少愚見을 敢陳ᄒᆞᆫ 것이 實노 創新的 意見이 아니오 卽是 經傳中에 具在ᄒᆞᆫ 光明寶라. 他求를 不待ᄒᆞ고 特其末流의 失을 救ᄒᆞ야 本面目을 回復코저 ᄒᆞᆷ이니 世之君子ᄂᆞᆫ 幸勿嗔恠ᄒᆞ고 平心以察ᄒᆞᆯ지어다. 蓋 過去 十九世紀와 現今二十世紀ᄂᆞᆫ 西洋文明이 大發達ᄒᆞᆫ 時期오 將來二十一二世紀ᄂᆞᆫ 東洋文明이 大發達ᄒᆞᆯ 時期니 吾 孔子의 道가 豈終墜地哉리오. 將次 全世界에 其 光輝ᄅᆞᆯ 大顯ᄒᆞᆯ 時斯가 有ᄒᆞᆯ지니 嗟呼라 我韓 儒林이여 明目以觀察ᄒᆞ고 奮身而擔着ᄒᆞᆯ지어다. 彼西洋敎界로 觀ᄒᆞᆯ지라도 羅馬舊敎時代ᄂᆞᆫ 卽 歐洲墨闇天地라. 萬一 馬丁路得의 大膽과 熱血로 改良求新ᄒᆞᆷ이 無ᄒᆞ얏스며 歐洲 日月이 至今ᄭᆞ지 黑闇中에 在ᄒᆞ야도 可ᄒᆞᆯ지라. 宗敎之於世運에 其 關係가 果何如哉아 我韓儒者의 結習은 改良이라 ᄒᆞ면 變事로 認ᄒᆞ나 天下之物이 大小ᄅᆞᆯ 莫論ᄒᆞ고 久則必弊오 弊則當改니 若弊而不改ᄒᆞ면 終焉熄滅而己니 可不念哉며 求新이라 ᄒᆞ면 別件으로 認ᄒᆞ나 新之一字ᄂᆞᆫ 吾道의 固有ᄒᆞᆫ 光明이라. 孔子ㅣ 曰 溫故而知新이라 ᄒᆞ시며 張子 曰 濯去舊見ᄒᆞ야 以來新意라 ᄒᆞ엿스니 道德은 以日新而輝光ᄒᆞ고 邦命은 以維新而增長ᄒᆞ나니 求新之義가 非自外來라. 嗟我儒林諸君이여.

paragraphs.en: Alas! In raising these views on the three great problems above, I have not put forward any truly novel opinion; it is the bright treasure that is present in the classics and commentaries. Without seeking elsewhere, I wish only to remedy the faults of its later currents and recover its original face. May the gentlemen of the world not be angry or find it strange, but examine it with a calm mind. The past nineteenth century and the present twentieth are the period of the great development of Western civilisation; the coming twenty-first and twenty-second centuries will be the period of the great development of Eastern civilisation, and how should the Way of our Confucius finally fall to the ground? There will come a time when its radiance shines greatly over the whole world. Alas, Confucians of Korea, open your eyes and observe, and rouse yourselves and shoulder the task! Look even at the Western religious world: the age of the old Roman faith was the dark, murky world of Europe. Had there not been Martin Luther's boldness and hot blood in reforming and renewing it, it would be fine for the sun and moon of Europe to remain even now in darkness. How great is the bearing of religion on the course of the world! The habit of Korean Confucians is to regard "reform" as an upheaval; but whatever thing under heaven, large or small, will in time inevitably decay, and what decays must be reformed; if it decays and is not reformed, it will in the end be extinguished. Should we not reflect on this? And they regard "renewal" as something alien; but the single word "new" is the bright light inherent in our Way. Confucius said, "Review the old and know the new"; Zhang Zai said, "Wash away old views so that new ideas may come." Moral virtue shines by renewing day by day, and the mandate of a state grows by renewal; the meaning of renewal does not come from outside. Alas, gentlemen of the Confucian community!
